title: Coordinated customer comms & RCA ticketing for autoscaler regression impact
creator: Aisha Raman
description: After the 2025-02-10 autoscaler regression that caused degraded throughput for several hosted tenants, we need an orchestrated post-incident effort: finalize the internal RCA, publish a customer-facing timeline and statuspage incident postmortem, and track remediation action items across runtime and control-plane teams. This ticket centralizes comms copy, PR links, assigned follow-ups, and verification steps for closure.
timeline:
2025-02-10 02:37 UTC: First alert - sustained queue growth on autoscale-controller.
2025-02-10 02:45 UTC: Pager duty oncall acknowledged, mitigation attempt (scale policy override) started.
2025-02-10 03:10 UTC: Temporary manual scales applied to affected pools; customer-facing flakiness observed until 03:40 UTC.
2025-02-10 04:05 UTC: Root cause identified as a tuple-change in recent autoscaler rollout (runtime-1.22) that reduced eligibility for burst pools under >95th percentile latency.
2025-02-11 09:00 UTC: Post-incident sync: agreement to delay further rollout and revert problematic policy while preparing fix.
2025-02-12 14:00 UTC: Draft customer email and statuspage copy authored and reviewed by PM and Legal.
2025-02-14 11:30 UTC: Engineering PR for fix merged behind feature flag (PR #1284).
2025-02-16 08:00 UTC: Canary validation completed in eu-west-1; monitoring shows normal throughput under load tests.
2025-02-18 16:00 UTC: Final review of public postmortem and scheduled statuspage publication for 2025-02-19 10:00 UTC.
rca_summary: Root cause: a behavioral change in the autoscale eligibility evaluator introduced in runtime-1.22 (commit abc123) changed scoring for burst-eligible nodes. The new heuristic excluded ~18% of previously eligible containers under high-latency tails, which prevented the autoscaler from provisioning burst capacity quickly enough to keep up with sudden load spikes. Contributing factors: insufficient load-scenario unit tests in the autoscaler CI matrix and an overly aggressive default eligibility threshold. Detection gap: internal synthetic monitors did not run at the high-percentile latency scenarios that triggered this regression.
statuspage_update: (Draft) Incident resolved — Autoscaler regression caused temporary throughput degradation for some hosted customers on 2025-02-10. We reverted the problematic policy and deployed a patch; full remediation completed and validated by 2025-02-16. Detailed postmortem and customer-facing timeline will be published at 2025-02-19 10:00 UTC. No customer data was compromised. We apologize for the disruption and are implementing safeguards to prevent recurrence.
customer_email_template:
Subject: Update on the 2025-02-10 service disruption

Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to follow up about the service degradation you may have seen on 2025-02-10. Summary: an autoscaler regression in a recent runtime change temporarily reduced burst capacity provisioning. Impact: increased request latency and reduced throughput for some jobs between ~02:30–03:40 UTC.

What we did: we reverted the change, deployed a fix behind a feature flag, and validated recovery across multiple regions.

What we are doing to prevent this: (1) add high-tail latency scenarios to autoscaler CI tests, (2) lower the default eligibility threshold and make it configurable per pool, (3) add an alert that triggers when eligibility drops >10% across a pool.

If you saw an incident impacting your application, please reply to this email or open a support ticket and reference case #INC-2025-02-Autoscale.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Reliability Team
